title: Orgwide engineering huddle — Sept 15 2026
content:
Meeting: Orgwide engineering huddle
Date: 2026-09-15 10:00–11:00 PT
Location: Zoom / Recorded in #eng-all-hands
Facilitator: Marcus Liu (Observability)
Attendees: ~120 engineering heads + rotating ICs (list appended in meeting recording)

TL;DR
- Short term focus: reduce p95 generation latency for small- and mid-length prompts and finish autoscaler policy rollout to Dedicated pools by Sept 28.
- Observability pilot: distributed KV-cache TTL change (from 2h -> 8h) in canary — early signals show 12% request token reduction for chat workloads.
- Two upcoming public-facing releases: SDK v0.9.7 (docs + streaming fixes) on Sept 22, and Console rollout for route-level cost breakdown on Sept 29.
- Major open risk: Q3 error-budget burn for Model A (base-16 quantized) due to regression after kernel update; hotfix expected by 9/18.

Agenda
1) Quick metrics snapshot (5m)
2) Team highlight: Observability (10m)
3) Cross-org coordination: Autoscaling / Dedicated (10m)
4) Serving runtime update: kernel selector + regression status (15m)
5) Product/Console: rollout plan and blocking items (10m)
6) Open Q&A and parking lot (10m)

1) Metrics snapshot (presented by Priya)
- P95 gen latency (hosted API): 142ms global (target 120ms). Improvement needed in EU small prompt tier.
- Error budget burn (last 14d): Model A 18% -> spike to 38% after 9/10 kernel push. SRE put Model A on degraded routing for priority customers.
- Dedicated pool utilization: avg 72% CPU/GPU utilization during peak hours; nights drop to 24%. Autoscaler active in 48% of pools.
- Average token cost (hosted): $0.032 / 1k tokens (weighted). Observability noted 4% delta with inference-side batching changes this week.

2) Observability highlight (Marcus)
- KV-cache TTL pilot: expanded the prefix/KV caching TTL in canary clusters to 8 hours for chat-typed workloads. Early results: 12% fewer model invocations, 9% lower p95 for chat continuity flows (measured across three customers).
- Rollout plan: continue canary through 9/22, add two more high-traffic tenants and synthetic tests, then scale to 30% traffic 9/24, full rollout 9/30 if no regressions.
- New tracing hooks: added a lightweight token-credit trace that surfaces per-request cache hits in Console traces. Live in staging; Documentation PR created (see linked artifacts).
- Ask to teams: please notify Observability if you plan changes to context-preserving features (chat history modifications) before 9/22 — TTL can amplify changes in correctness tests.

3) Autoscaling & Dedicated capacity (Dana)
- Autoscaler policy: global autoscaler v1.4 with scale-in cool-down reduced from 10m -> 3m to match burst traffic patterns. This reduces underutilized warm nodes but slightly raises transient scale events.- Canary: applied to 14 Dedicated pools; measured 7% improvement in request tail latency during bursts and 4% cost improvement for reserved capacity customers.
- Burst capacity test scheduled: 9/23 02:00–04:00 PT. Runbook in Confluence. All teams with Dedicated pools should sign up for rollback authority if they rely on stable latency SLAs during that window.
- Action: Platform engineering to run a simulated failover across two regions the week of 9/20. ETA for report: 9/27.

4) Serving runtime update (Sofia)
- Kernel selector improvements landed in runtime main; this reduced median GPU time for long sequences by ~6% in lab tests. However, a kernel mismap after the 9/10 push caused regressions for Model A on some quantized paths.- Recovery: engineering identified a misapplied transformation in the attention kernel for quantized models. A targeted hotfix PR (runtime#789) will be merged by EOD 9/16 and deployed to canaries 9/17.
- Regression mitigation: fallback policy added that routes affected requests to the previous kernel variant until hotfix is validated. This has reduced customer-facing errors by ~55% since 9/12.
- Longer-term: introduce per-model kernel validation jobs in CI that run on representative input shapes; RFC due by 9/29.

5) Product/Console update (Liam)
- Console: route-level cost breakdown feature is in final QA. Rolling rollout plan: 10% of users 9/29, 50% 10/06, 100% 10/13.- Known blocker: some orgs with heavy legacy usage patterns experience slow dashboard queries; backend index tuning is in flight. Expected patch 9/21.- UX change: added a toggle to show token-level cost deltas for routes (opt-in). Please review UX mocks in Confluence.
- SDK: v0.9.7 will address streaming re-connection edge cases and add typed function-calling helpers. Release branch created; docs freeze 9/20, release 9/22.

6) Open Q&A / Parking lot
- Q: Any ETA on model refresh cadence for the hosted catalog? A: Research is finalizing a quarterly cadence proposal; first scheduled refresh window is Oct 12–16.
- Q: How do private deployments get kernel updates? A: Private will continue to receive tested runtime packages on a separate tracked schedule; we are shipping the hotfix to the private channel after verifying customer-specific tests (expected week of 9/20).
- Parking lot items: discuss trial of per-tenant model pruning to save costs (move to architecture forum), refine long-tail prompt TL;DR heuristics, and finalize the SRE on-call rotation changes (HR discussion ongoing).

Decisions made in meeting
- Approve extended KV-cache TTL canary (8h) through 9/22 and staged rollout if no regressions.
- Proceed with autoscaler v1.4 canary for all Dedicated pools and run the scheduled burst capacity test on 9/23.
- Serve hotfix for Model A in canary 9/17 and to wider fleet after verification (target 9/18–9/19).

Action items (owner — due)
- Runtime: merge and deploy hotfix PR runtime#789 to canary clusters (Sofia) — due 2026-09-17.
- Observability: add two high-traffic tenants to KV-cache TTL canary and run synthetic regression suite (Marcus) — due 2026-09-22.
- Platform: complete region failover simulation and produce report (Dana) — due 2026-09-27.
- Product: fix Console slow-query indexing and finish QA for route-level cost breakdown (Liam) — due 2026-09-21.
- SDK: finalize docs and publish v0.9.7 (Priya) — due 2026-09-22.
- SRE: prepare outage runbook and rollback authority list for 9/23 burst capacity test (SRE leads) — due 2026-09-20.

Shoutouts
- Kudos to the runtime team (esp. Anika and Raj) for quickly isolating the attention-kernel mismatch and producing the hotfix patch.
- Observability infra: new trace sampling reduction cut ingestion costs in staging by 8% — nice work.

Notes / Context / Links
- Recording and full attendee list: see Confluence deck (linked).
- Related Jira: ENG-4123 (kernel regression triage), ENG-4197 (autoscaler rollout), ENG-4220 (console cost breakdown QA).
- Internal docs: KV-cache TTL proposal page (linked), runtime PR 789 for hotfix.

Next meeting
- Orgwide huddle: Sept 29, 10:00–11:00 PT. Focus: post-burst-test review, hotfix validation, and Q4 roadmap touchpoints.

If you are assigned an action item above and need help reprioritizing, ping me or drop a note in #eng-ops.

-- Marcus
Observability
